title: SAT 15 · Equivalent fractions
description: A/B reasoning practice. Difficulty is editorial, not standardized SAT calibration.

questions.title: Equivalent Name for Two Thirds
questions.learningObjective: Apply equivalent fractions and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: A fraction card shows \(\frac23\). Which fraction has the same value? Choose A or B and explain how the numerator and denominator change.
questions.explanation: Multiplying both the numerator and denominator of \(\frac23\) by \(2\) gives \(\frac{2\times2}{3\times2}=\frac46\), so the value does not change. The fraction \(\frac45\) is different: with denominator 15, \(\frac23=\frac{10}{15}\) and \(\frac45=\frac{12}{15}\). Therefore, \(\frac46\) is equivalent to \(\frac23\), while \(\frac45\) is not.

visuals.alt: A table lists card P as 2/3, card Q as 4/6, and card R as 4/5.

questions.hint: Look for a number that multiplies both the numerator and the denominator of 2/3; the table lists the cards.

questions.title: Comparing Two Bottle Fractions
questions.learningObjective: Apply equivalent fractions and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: One bottle contains \(\frac34\) liter of water and another contains \(\frac58\) liter. Which bottle contains more water? Choose A or B and justify the comparison.
questions.explanation: Rewrite \(\frac34\) with denominator 8: \(\frac34=\frac68\). Since \(\frac68>\frac58\), the bottle containing \(\frac34\) liter has more water. The other choice is smaller by \(\frac18\) liter.

visuals.alt: A number line from 0 to 1 marks 5/8 at 0.625 and 3/4 at 0.75; 3/4 lies to the right of 5/8.

questions.hint: Rewrite one fraction so both have denominator 8, or compare their positions on the number line.

questions.title: Finding a Missing Numerator
questions.learningObjective: Apply equivalent fractions and justify the selected answer.
questions.question:
What whole number \(n\) makes the fractions equivalent? Choose A or B and explain how you find the missing numerator.
\[\frac35=\frac{n}{20}\]
questions.explanation: The denominator changes from 5 to 20 by multiplication by 4. To keep the fraction equivalent, multiply the numerator by the same factor: \(3\times4=12\). Thus \(\frac35=\frac{12}{20}\), not \(\frac{15}{20}\). Multiplying both parts of \(\frac35\) by 1, 2, 3, and 4 gives the equivalent fractions \(\frac35\), \(\frac6{10}\), \(\frac9{15}\), and \(\frac{12}{20}\).
questions.hint: Find what the denominator 5 was multiplied by to reach 20, and apply the same factor to the numerator.

questions.title: Recognizing Equal Fraction Values
questions.learningObjective: Apply equivalent fractions and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Which statement correctly compares \(\frac26\) and \(\frac13\)? Choose A or B and justify your choice by simplifying one fraction.
questions.explanation: Dividing the numerator and denominator of \(\frac26\) by 2 gives \(\frac{2\div2}{6\div2}=\frac13\). Both fractions represent the same amount. Therefore, the statement that \(\frac26\) is greater is incorrect.
questions.hint: Simplify 2/6 by dividing its numerator and denominator by their common factor.

questions.title: Comparing Fractions with a Common Denominator
questions.learningObjective: Apply equivalent fractions and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Which fraction is larger, \(\frac7{12}\) or \(\frac35\)? Use the table to compare them after writing both with denominator 60.
questions.explanation: Because \(\frac7{12}=\frac{35}{60}\) and \(\frac35=\frac{36}{60}\), both fractions have the same denominator and can be compared by their numerators. Since \(36>35\), \(\frac35\) is larger. The first fraction is smaller by \(\frac1{60}\).

visuals.alt: A table shows 7/12 as 35/60 and 3/5 as 36/60.

questions.hint: Use the table's denominator-60 forms and compare the numerators.

questions.title: Recovering a Denominator
questions.learningObjective: Apply equivalent fractions and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: The fractions \(\frac{18}{24}\) and \(\frac3d\) are equivalent. What is the value of \(d\)? Choose A or B and show how you simplify the first fraction.
questions.explanation: Divide both 18 and 24 by 6 to simplify \(\frac{18}{24}=\frac34\). For \(\frac3d\) to equal \(\frac34\), its denominator must be 4. If \(d=5\), the fraction would be \(\frac35\), which is not equal to \(\frac34\).
questions.hint: Simplify 18/24 completely, then match the numerators to find d.

questions.title: A Fraction Between Two Bounds
questions.learningObjective: Apply equivalent fractions and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Which fraction lies strictly between \(\frac23\) and \(\frac34\)? Choose A or B and justify that it is greater than the lower bound and less than the upper bound.
questions.explanation: Use a common denominator of 60: \(\frac23=\frac{40}{60}\), \(\frac7{10}=\frac{42}{60}\), and \(\frac34=\frac{45}{60}\). Since \(40<42<45\), \(\frac7{10}\) is strictly between the two bounds. The other fraction, \(\frac45=\frac{48}{60}\), is greater than \(\frac34\).
questions.hint: Rewrite all the fractions with one common denominator, such as 60, and check which option lies between the bounds.

questions.title: Simplifying Fourteen Thirty-Fifths
questions.learningObjective: Apply equivalent fractions and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Which fraction is equivalent to \(\frac{14}{35}\)? Choose A or B and explain how the numerator and denominator can be reduced by the same factor.
questions.explanation: The greatest common factor of 14 and 35 is 7. Dividing both by 7 gives \(\frac{14}{35}=\frac25\). The fraction \(\frac35\) is larger because, with denominator 35, it equals \(\frac{21}{35}\), not \(\frac{14}{35}\). Equivalently, scaling \(\frac25\) by 1, 2, 3, and 7 gives \(\frac25\), \(\frac4{10}\), \(\frac6{15}\), and \(\frac{14}{35}\).
questions.hint: Find the greatest common factor of 14 and 35 and divide both parts by it.

questions.title: Solving for a Fraction Parameter
questions.learningObjective: Apply equivalent fractions and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Assume \(k+1\ne0\) and \(\frac{3}{k+1}=\frac14\). What is \(k\)? Choose A or B and show how the equality determines the denominator.
questions.explanation: For \(\frac{3}{k+1}\) to equal \(\frac14\), the denominator must be four times the numerator: \(k+1=3\times4=12\). Therefore, \(k=11\). If \(k=12\), the fraction would be \(\frac3{13}\), which is not \(\frac14\).
questions.hint: Ask what the denominator must be so that 3 divided by it equals 1/4, then solve for k.

questions.title: Comparing a Variable Fraction with One-Half
questions.learningObjective: Apply equivalent fractions and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: For every positive integer \(n\), how does \(\frac{n+1}{2n+3}\) compare with \(\frac12\)? Choose A or B and justify the inequality without substituting particular values of \(n\).
questions.explanation: Since \(n\) is positive, the denominator \(2n+3\) is positive. Comparing the fraction with \(\frac12\) is therefore equivalent to comparing \(2(n+1)\) with \(2n+3\). But \(2n+2<2n+3\), so the fraction is always less than \(\frac12\). The claim that it is greater is false for every allowed value of \(n\).
questions.hint: Since the denominator is positive, compare 2(n+1) with 2n+3 instead of comparing the fractions directly.

questions.title: Solving an Equation of Equivalent Fractions
questions.learningObjective: Apply equivalent fractions and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: The denominator \(5x+1\) is nonzero and \(\frac{3x+2}{5x+1}=\frac23\). What is \(x\)? Choose A or B and show the cross-multiplication steps.
questions.explanation: Cross-multiply to get \(3(3x+2)=2(5x+1)\). Expanding gives \(9x+6=10x+2\), so \(x=4\). Substitution gives \(\frac{3(4)+2}{5(4)+1}=\frac{14}{21}=\frac23\). For \(x=-4\), the fraction is \(\frac{-10}{-19}=\frac{10}{19}\), not \(\frac23\).
questions.hint: Cross-multiply, expand both sides, and solve the linear equation; then substitute to check.

questions.title: A Difference That Equals Seven Twelfths
questions.learningObjective: Apply equivalent fractions and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes \(\frac56-\frac14\)? Choose A or B and show how a common denominator resolves the comparison.
questions.explanation: Using denominator 12 gives \(\frac56=\frac{10}{12}\) and \(\frac14=\frac3{12}\). Their difference is \(\frac{10}{12}-\frac3{12}=\frac7{12}\), exactly the stated fraction. The result is equal to, not greater than, \(\frac7{12}\).
questions.hint: Rewrite both fractions with denominator 12 before subtracting.

questions.title: Enough Ribbon After Adding a Piece
questions.learningObjective: Apply equivalent fractions and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Lina needs \(\frac34\) meter of ribbon for a craft. She has a piece that is \(\frac23\) meter long and adds another piece that is \(\frac16\) meter long. Does she have enough ribbon, and how much is left over or still needed? Choose A or B and justify both the total length and the comparison.

options.label: A
options.text: Lina has enough, with \(\frac1{12}\) meter left.

questions.explanation: First add the two pieces: \(\frac23+\frac16=\frac46+\frac16=\frac56\) meter. Compare this with the required \(\frac34\) meter by using denominator 12: \(\frac56=\frac{10}{12}\) and \(\frac34=\frac9{12}\). Lina has \(\frac{10}{12}-\frac9{12}=\frac1{12}\) meter more than she needs, so she is not short.
questions.hint: Add the two pieces using a common denominator, then compare the total with 3/4 using denominator 12.

questions.title: Counting Equivalent Fraction Cards
questions.learningObjective: Apply equivalent fractions and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: A set of four fraction cards shows the values in the table. How many cards are equivalent to \(\frac34\), counting the card that already shows \(\frac34\)? Choose A or B and explain how you check each card.
questions.explanation: The first three cards are equivalent: \(\frac34\) is the reference fraction, \(\frac68\) simplifies to \(\frac34\) by dividing its numerator and denominator by 2, and \(\frac9{12}\) simplifies to \(\frac34\) by dividing both terms by 3. However, \(\frac{10}{16}\) simplifies to \(\frac58\), so it is not equivalent to \(\frac34\). Therefore, exactly three cards match.

visuals.alt: Four cards show P as 3/4, Q as 6/8, R as 9/12, and S as 10/16.

questions.hint: Simplify each card's fraction to lowest terms and compare it with 3/4.

questions.title: Solving an Equivalent-Fraction Equation
questions.learningObjective: Apply equivalent fractions and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: For what value of \(x\) are the fractions \(\frac{2x-1}{3x+4}\) and \(\frac35\) equivalent? Assume \(3x+4\ne0\). Choose A or B and show how cross-multiplication gives the value.
questions.explanation: Set the cross-products equal: \(5(2x-1)=3(3x+4)\). This gives \(10x-5=9x+12\), so \(x=17\). Substituting gives \(\frac{2(17)-1}{3(17)+4}=\frac{33}{55}=\frac35\). At \(x=7\), the fraction is \(\frac{13}{25}\), which is not equivalent to \(\frac35\).
questions.hint: Set the cross-products equal, solve for x, and check by substituting back.

questions.title: Finding a Tank's Capacity from Two Fractions
questions.learningObjective: Apply equivalent fractions and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: A tank is \(\frac58\) full. After 6 liters of water are added, it is \(\frac34\) full. What is the tank's total capacity? Use the table to identify the fraction of the tank represented by the 6 liters.
questions.explanation: Write \(\frac34\) as \(\frac68\). The amount added changes the tank from \(\frac58\) to \(\frac68\), so 6 liters represents \(\frac18\) of the tank. The full capacity is \(6\times8=48\) liters. A capacity of 24 liters would make \(\frac18\) equal to 3 liters, not 6 liters.

visuals.alt: A table shows that the tank is 5/8 full before adding water and 3/4 full afterward, when 6 liters have been added.

questions.hint: Write 3/4 in eighths using the table; the 6 liters fill the difference between the two fractions.

questions.title: Comparing a Parameterized Fraction with Three-Fifths
questions.learningObjective: Apply equivalent fractions and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Let \(n\) be a positive integer. Which statement correctly compares \(\frac{n+2}{2n+3}\) with \(\frac35\) for all allowed values of \(n\)? Choose A or B and justify your conclusion by comparing cross-products and checking the boundary case.

options.label: B
options.text: It equals \(\frac35\) when \(n=1\) and is less than \(\frac35\) for every integer \(n>1\).

questions.explanation: The denominator \(2n+3\) is positive. Compare the cross-products \(5(n+2)=5n+10\) and \(3(2n+3)=6n+9\). Their difference, first minus second, is \(1-n\). It is zero when \(n=1\), so the fractions are equal in that case. For every integer \(n>1\), the difference is negative, so \(\frac{n+2}{2n+3}<\frac35\). The first statement fails at \(n=1\).
questions.hint: Compare the cross-products 5(n+2) and 3(2n+3); look at their difference and test the smallest allowed n.

questions.title: A Necessary Ratio from Equivalent Fractions
questions.learningObjective: Apply equivalent fractions and justify the selected answer.
questions.question: Let \(a\) and \(b\) be positive integers. If \(\frac ab=\frac{a+3}{b+5}\), which ratio must \(\frac ab\) equal? Choose A or B and derive the result from the equality.
questions.explanation: Since the fractions are equal and the denominators are positive, cross-multiplication gives \(a(b+5)=b(a+3)\). Expanding yields \(ab+5a=ab+3b\), so \(5a=3b\). Dividing both sides by \(5b\) gives \(\frac ab=\frac35\). The reciprocal \(\frac53\) does not follow from the equation and reverses the required ratio.
questions.hint: Cross-multiply and expand both sides; the ab terms cancel, leaving a relation between a and b.
